newsitem.title: UK: Closing stock market indices -- May 21.
newsitem.headline: Closing stock market indices -- May 21.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - UK shares pushed back to within striking distance of their record closing levels as investors on both sides of the Atlantic celebrated the U.S. central bank's decision to leave U.S. interest rates at current levels. The FTSE 100 index ended 34.5 points firmer at 4,642.0.

FRANKFURT - The German DAX index held gains to end the bourse session up 1.5 percent, buoyed by surprise at the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave rates unchanged, with the outlook for after-bourse trade seen hinging on Wall Street opening but mood positive. The DAX index closed up 52.66 points at 3,596.09. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,600.40.

PARIS - French shares recovered all of Tuesday's losses and made some headway, as the market welcomed the benign outlook for U.S. interest rates, the CAC index regained the 2,800 level hit last week was unable to hold the gains amid profit-taking. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 35.24 points or 1.28 percent at 2,786.35. ZURICH - Swiss shares resumed their bull run, jumping nearly two percent to reach a new record close on the back of steady U.S interest rates and an easing Swiss franc. The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) advanced 54.07 points or 1.68 percent to 3,268.35.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks stumbled late in afternoon trade to end more than two percent lower, rattled by comments by the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) deputy governor that the central bank is considering the right timing to raise the official discount rate. The 225-share Nikkei average finished 490.85 points or 2.41 percent lower at 19,841.98.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks surrendered early gains and closed marginally lower as profit-taking emerged after the market digested news U.S. interest rates had been left unchanged. The Hang Seng Index was down 0.68 of a point to close at 14,235.52.

SYDNEY - A resurgent banking sector, encouraged by news of unchanged U.S. interest rates, carried the Australian stock market to a record close. with buyers coming back into the market looking for a bargain, in particular the banks. The All Ordinaries Index closed up 12.5 points to 2,543.2.

JOHANNESBURG - South African stocks ended up amid wide relief that the Federal Reserve had decided to hold United States interest rates steady, The rates decision on Tuesday came as a pleasent surprise to most market players as speculation had been rife for a 25 basis point rise. The All-share index added 21.0 points to 7,127.2, Industrials put on 24.2 points to finish at 8,396.2 and golds gained 0.4 points to 1,213.7.
